analysis.title: BOJ – Hawks Are Taking Over
key_insights: The BoJ meeting on 30 Oct 2026 was notable for the absence of dissent. Asada and Sato, the Takaichi appointees who voted against a hike in September citing below-target inflation and consumption concerns, did not dissent.

Governor Ueda said the committee unanimously agreed that underlying inflation was generally consistent with the 2% target for the first time. Two doves who had projected 2% CPI in 2028 with downside risk moved to neutral.

TS Lombard reads the shift in Asada and Sato's stance as a continued move under Takaichi away from her preference for lower rates and a weaker yen. It calls this the right decision, since BoJ forecasts and its dot plot have inflation at or above target through 2029.

Ueda describes a new phase of monetary policy focused on anchoring inflation and the degree of financial accommodation. The statement, the presser, the BoJ's CPI measure excluding institutional factors and the Financial System Report together indicate the BoJ sees rates as overly accommodative and the risk of overshooting its inflation target as material.
Ueda did not commit to a December hike but said every meeting is live, noted the need for vigilance on overshooting, and said 'we will not just sit and wait' for inflation to become anchored.
TS Lombard expects BoJ hikes in December, March and July, taking rates to 2%, followed by a pause to assess the impact of tightening.

The BoJ announced it will accelerate its equity (ETF) disposal. The sale will now take 43 years, against the previous estimate of 112 years. Funds transferred to the Ministry of Finance are projected at roughly 0.7% of next year's budget.
TS Lombard says markets are generally underpricing BoJ hawkishness. A December hike is priced at 81% and the terminal rate at 1.9%, against a consensus terminal rate of 1.75%.
TS Lombard remains positive on the yen and expects returning Japanese capital could help long-end JGBs outperform developed-market rates.
